description: BetFirm review, checked 20 Nov 2026: Jack Jones's pick storefront, prices from $29.99 to $1,999.95 a year, its own leaderboards checked, and buyer reports.
dek: A picks and betting articles site that says Jack Jones founded it in 2003. It lists about 29 handicappers, led by Jones, and every Buy Now button sends you to the SportsCapping.com cart. Prices run from $29.99 for one pick to $1,999.95 for a year, guarantees pay in free picks, not cash, and its leaderboards come from the same network that sells the picks and show no handicapper in the red.

short_answer: BetFirm is a working storefront with a long history. A 2004 saved copy shows BetFirms.com relaunching as a gambling information site, and by 2016 BetFirm.com was selling Jack Jones's picks much as it does today. It posts prices, shows each handicapper's plays from the day before with the result, and hands buyers to the SportsCapping.com checkout, which names Boyd Information Group as its billing company. BetFirm itself names no company, address or phone number, and we found no terms or refund page on the site.

We set its sales copy against its own leaderboards. Some headline claims match: Jones is No. 2 on BetFirm's all time table and No. 1 on its all time NBA table. Others do not: a "#2 NFL All-Time" claim sits next to a table that ranks him third, and "Totals Guru Top MLB Expert" appears on neither MLB table. This year Jones is up $636 on $100 bets across 1,734 graded picks, a 0.3% return, less than a third of the $1,999.95 price of his yearly pass.

Every row on every BetFirm leaderboard we opened showed a profit, although the page says it lists "all of our handicappers". We found almost no independent buyer talk about BetFirm itself: one 2013 forum member praised Jones's free picks, and a TheRX member reposted his plays in 2026. Treat it as a store with marketing records, not a source of proven winners.

guarantee: BetFirm's guarantee wording is sales copy on each package. The 7 day pass says: "You are GUARANTEED PROFITS or the next 7 days of premium picks in all sports is ON JACK!" The 365 day pass says Jack "GUARANTEES it or the next 365 days of premium picks in all sports is ON JACK!" In plain words, if a pass loses you get another pass of the same length. You do not get your money back, and it never covers what you lost on the bets.

Because the period that follows a losing period comes from the same handicapper, a buyer who loses can end up with more of the picks that lost. The 3 day pass carried no guarantee wording at all on 20 Nov 2026.

Because checkout happens on SportsCapping.com, the SportsCapping rules apply. When we read its FAQ on 17 Nov 2026 it said "refunds are reviewed individually", that losing guaranteed packages earn a free replacement on their own, and that credits "can't be withdrawn or exchanged for cash." Its Terms of Use provide the service "as is", send disputes to courts in Iowa and limit claims to one year. Both pages loaded only as a blank app shell on 20 Nov 2026, so we could not re-read them today.

claims_note: How we checked: on 20 Nov 2026 we opened BetFirm's overall, NBA, MLB, NFL and college football leaderboards, each with a current season table and an all time "Top Trends" table, and set the sales copy beside them. These tables come from the SportsCapping network that sells the picks, so a match means the sales copy agrees with the seller's own scoreboard, not that an outsider verified it.

The overall page says it shows "the documented records for all of our handicappers for the current year." It listed 29 names, all in profit, while the NBA table names others such as Kevin Young, whom the page's own FAQ calls one of the best handicappers in the world, yet who is absent from the overall table. That suggests handicappers below zero are left out, though the page does not say so.

Profit is shown in dollars on $100 bets and does not subtract the price of the picks. Jones's line this year, +$636 on $100 bets, would leave a $100 bettor about $1,364 behind after a $1,999.95 yearly pass. A $1,000 bettor would be about $4,360 ahead before fees, at a 0.3% return on roughly $1.7 million wagered.

The runs move by the day. The headline run changed between our 17 Nov and 20 Nov visits, and the window ("L3357 Days") is chosen by the seller. A record that begins on a chosen date can always be made to look good.
record: Watchdog graded sample, new 22 Nov 2026. BetFirm does not publish a complete, time stamped log we can audit, so we built a sample from public posts that carry their plays. Watchdog captures X accounts and forum threads that post or repost picks; the ones naming BetFirm most often were AA_PocketRockets, gojuicd. From 21 Oct 2026 to 21 Oct 2026 we took every play our parser could read inside a BetFirm block, kept only those posted before the game started, removed repeats, and graded each one against the final score at one unit risked, at the odds shown or -110 when none were shown.
Result: 1 plays, 1 won, 0 lost, +0.91 units, a return of +90.9% per unit risked. By sport: too few per sport to split. By month: October 1 won, 0 lost, +0.91 units.

What it means: 1 decided plays is far too few to judge. We list them so readers can see what was posted and how it did; the sample covers only plays others chose to post, not the full card a subscriber receives.
What a buyer can verify independently: nothing we could find. We found no full, time stamped log kept by an outside monitor and no contest result we could open.

What BetFirm publishes: leaderboards by sport, each with a current season table and an all time table, plus a yesterday's plays table on each handicapper page. On 20 Nov 2026 Jones's table showed his 20* Texans -11.5 play from the night before as a win. The tables use the SportsCapping "Sc Score" column, so the numbers come from the selling network.

Taken at face value, the network's own numbers show thin margins. Jones's all time line, 10,557-9,364, is 53.0% winners and a 1.83% return. On the current overall table the 29 handicappers shown range from 48.0% to 57.5% winners, and only 3 of them return more than 5%.

History: the betfirm.com domain record shows a 27 Dec 2003 registration. A saved copy of BetFirms.com from 16 Jan 2004 announced that "PlayADaySports.com will be re-branded as BetFirms.com" on 1 Feb 2004, offering free picks "from over 80 sports services" and gambling articles. By Jan 2016 BetFirm.com was selling Jack Jones's picks and called him "the No. 1 Ranked Basketball Handicapper All-Time on this network."

customers_intro: We found almost no independent buyer review of BetFirm. CapperTek lists both BetFirm.com and BetFirms.com with no reviews, re-checked on 20 Nov 2026. A Reddit archive search of r/sportsbetting on 20 Nov 2026 returned one post, which used the word in an unrelated question; other subreddit queries timed out, so we also relied on our earlier Reddit downloads. Web searches of Sportsbook Review, Covers and TheRX found two relevant posts. The entries below are what exists.

customers.text: There is almost no buyer talk about BetFirm as a business, positive or negative, across 13 years of forum posts. Review sites list it with zero reviews, we found no Reddit post about it, no forum thread reviewing it and no news coverage. Two outside mentions exist, both about Jack Jones rather than BetFirm: a Sportsbook Review member in June 2013 said they started out with Jack Jones's free picks and found him "pretty good", and a TheRX member reposted his plays in April 2026 without comment. The checkout company, Boyd Information Group, had one BBB complaint on file. With so little buyer evidence, the record question rests on the network's own numbers, which show thin margins.

In a Sportsbook Review thread asking whether anyone makes money from free picks, a member said they had started out following Jack Jones's free picks and others on Twitter, and that Jones was pretty good. The post does not mention BetFirm or a purchase.
A member of a TheRX daily plays thread posted seven Jack Jones plays for the day with their star ratings. The post gives no view on his results or on buying from BetFirm.

BBB lists Boyd Information Group, the company named by the SportsCapping checkout, as not rated and in business less than six months under that file, opened 29 Sep 2026, with one complaint in the last three years and no customer reviews. BBB does not show the complaint text, so we cannot say whether it involved a BetFirm purchase.

CapperTek lists BetFirm.com and BetFirms.com, both with no reviews or complaints. We found no Sportsbook Review, Covers or TheRX thread reviewing BetFirm, no BBB profile under the BetFirm name and no news coverage, and we did not read Trustpilot.

conflicts: BetFirm's founder is also its top selling handicapper and its editor in chief, and its rankings come from the SportsCapping network that processes the sales. Every link in the chain earns from the sale.
Buy Now links carry an affiliate code into the SportsCapping cart, so BetFirm is paid as a referral storefront for the network.
BetFirm names no company of its own. A buyer with a problem has to deal with SportsCapping and Boyd Information Group, which the BetFirm pages do not explain.
BetFirm's leaderboards present only handicappers in profit and label the result "documented records", while the rankings, the grading and the checkout all sit inside the same network.
strengths: Prices are posted for every package, and the site has run under the same name for more than 20 years.
Each handicapper page shows yesterday's plays with the result, losses included.
Leaderboards show win rate, ROI and record side by side, and several headline claims (Jones No. 2 overall, No. 1 NBA, No. 3 college football) match them.
Lots of free material: a daily free pick, betting guides and odds pages.
The checkout company has a BBB file showing one complaint in the last three years.
concerns: No company name, address, phone, terms or refund page on BetFirm itself.
Records and rankings come from the network that sells the picks, and every row shown is in profit. No outside monitor found.
Some sales claims do not match BetFirm's own tables, such as "#2 NFL All-Time" (table: No. 3) and "Totals Guru Top MLB Expert" (not listed).
Sales copy leans on long chosen runs, while this year's table shows Jones at a 0.3% return, less than a yearly pass costs a $100 bettor.
Guarantees pay in more picks from the same handicapper, not cash.
Almost no independent buyer reviews, positive or negative.
checklist: Open the handicapper's current season row on BetFirm's leaderboard, not the run in the sales copy, and note the ROI.
Subtract the price of the picks from any profit figure before you compare. At $100 a game, most rows shown earn less than a yearly pass costs.
Ask for every pick from the last 12 months with the line, odds and send time. A long run with a chosen start date is not a record.
Read each package's guarantee line. Not every pass has one, and none pays cash.
Know that your card statement and any dispute go through SportsCapping and Boyd Information Group, not BetFirm.
Write down each pick yourself the moment you receive it, with the line you can actually get.
Give any handicapper a few hundred picks before you call them a winner.
faq: It is a long running storefront that delivers picks through the SportsCapping.com checkout, and it says Jack Jones founded it in 2003. It names no company of its own, and we could not verify that its handicappers win over time, because the records come from the network that sells the picks.
What does the Watchdog sample of BetFirm show?
We graded 1 of their plays that were posted publicly before the game started, 21 Oct 2026 to 21 Oct 2026: 1 won, 0 lost, +0.91 units at one unit each. That is too few plays to judge.
On 20 Nov 2026 Jack Jones single plays cost $39.95 to $49.95, a 1 day pass $59.95 and a 365 day pass $1,999.95. Bobby Conn plays started at $29.99 and his season passes ran from $125.00 to $899.99.

The About page says Jack Jones established it in 2003 and lists him as editor in chief. Payments go through SportsCapping.com, whose FAQ says purchases show on card statements as Boyd Information Group.

Several of Jack Jones's headline ranks match BetFirm's own tables, but some claims do not, and every row on those tables shows a profit. The tables are kept by the network that sells the picks, not by an outside monitor.

BetFirm shows no refund policy. Its guarantees give you another period of picks if a pass loses. The SportsCapping checkout FAQ said refunds are "reviewed individually" and credits cannot be exchanged for cash.

Only if a handicapper shows a profit over hundreds of picks after the price of the picks. Jones's own current year line on the site was up $636 on $100 bets, about a 0.3% return, before paying for the picks.
